To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) international doctoral students and staff at the University of Cambridge and University of Oxford experience difficulties in acculturating into UK academic practice, 2) these difficulties are related to differences in the ways in which UK and non-UK academics conceptualise academic practice and 3) these difficulties are compounded by the lack of a shared understanding of the role of doctoral education in the development of academic practice and by the lack of opportunities for international staff and students to learn about UK academic practice.

the experiences of international students and academic staff were similar in that they all faced challenges of acculturation into UK academia, but the experiences were also different, with the students having a stronger sense of being an ‘outsider’ in the academic culture.

international students and staff in the UK experience a variety of challenges when acculturating into academic practice, which include: 1) the lack of awareness of what is required in the UK; 2)  the lack of knowledge of the UK system; 3) the lack of knowledge about the expectations of academic staff and students; 4) the lack of support and resources; and 5) the lack of social support.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the process of acculturation into UK doctoral and academic practice, as experienced by international doctoral students and staff.
the process of acculturation of international doctoral researchers into the UK research culture.
understanding the ways in which international doctoral students and international academic staff experience and negotiate the process of acculturation into academic practice in the UK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the experiences of both international doctoral students and international academic staff in the two UK universities are similar in that they are both experiencing the challenges of acculturation into UK academia.
the international students who participated in this research were able to acculturate to the academic practices of UK research intensive universities.

international PhD students and academic staff in the UK have different experiences and perceptions of acculturation into UK academia and that these are influenced by their cultural backgrounds and the type of academic institution in which they are based.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and tested an instrument that measures the extent to which students have acculturated into UK academic practices, that we have developed a typology of acculturation and that we have developed an understanding of the role of the supervisor in the acculturation process.
we have been successful in developing a new model of academic development that is more responsive to the needs of the academic staff.
we are trying to understand the experiences of international students and staff as they acculturate into UK higher education, with the aim of improving their experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the international student experience is not a singular, uniform experience.
international doctoral students and early career academic staff are not a homogenous group.
international students are often more successful than native students in terms of their academic performance.
